resources.string: A minimal two-hour precipitation forecast. Tap to refresh. Touch and hold for widget settings.
Precipitation forecast. Open Rainline to choose a location.
The rainfall scale is 0–%1$s mm/h. Guides mark %2$s and %3$s mm/h; a small upward mark means rain exceeds the scale.

A dotted part of the axis has no forecast data. An open ring means waiting for data; a refresh arrow means data could not be obtained. Tap the widget to retry.\n\nStored forecasts stay visible while they contain any valid intervals in the next 90 minutes. The two-hour axis advances with the current time, leaving missing intervals empty.
MET is retiring this API version. Check for a Rainline update.

Rainline uses your location during forecast updates so the widget follows you even when the app is closed.

The coordinates are sent directly to MET Norway to fetch local weather. Rainline stores the selected location and a small weather cache on this device, with no analytics or tracking service.

Choose “%1$s” in Android’s Location permission screen. Background access is an option inside Location, not a separate permission in the list.

If Android no longer shows a permission request, use App settings → Permissions → Location. You can keep using a fixed place without this permission.
Sample precipitation graph. Appearance preview only.
Tap the widget to refresh it. Android’s power saving can delay automatic updates, so the forecast may not update immediately when you wake your phone.
Status: disabled\nTap to enable following from the home screen
Without background access, the saved position is used for up to two hours. After that, open Rainline for a fresh position or use a fixed place. A fixed place updates without location permission.
This location is approximate. Precise location gives a more local rain forecast.

Rain anywhere in the next two hours uses the rain interval. The slower dry interval needs at least 90 minutes of continuous dry data; missing data uses the rain interval. Intervals start at the last successful server check and also apply after wake or unlock. The graph can advance without downloading data. Updates pause while locked or asleep, and Android may delay them. Refresh now checks sooner while respecting the weather service’s cache.

Based on data from MET Norway, licensed under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0.\n\nRainline draws the precipitation rates as a line, interpolates between samples, and crops the forecast to the next two hours. It is an independent app and is not endorsed by MET Norway, Yr or NRK.
Preview and copy a local summary

The complete source code is included alongside this test APK.

Rainline has no accounts, ads, analytics or tracking SDKs.

Forecast requests send coordinates rounded to four decimals directly to api.met.no over HTTPS. MET Norway records IP addresses and request coordinates in its API access logs.

Location access is optional: you can enter a fixed place or coordinates. Following your location while the app is closed requires optional background location access.

Place-name searches use Android’s geocoding service. Its provider receives your search text; entering coordinates avoids that search.

Settings and a small cache of recent forecast locations are stored on your device. Rainline excludes these from cloud backup and device transfer. Uninstalling clears them.

Diagnostics are generated locally. Copy places the displayed technical summary on the clipboard; Rainline never uploads it.

Rainline is open-source software under the MIT licence.

Eight digits put opacity first: 00 is transparent, FF is opaque. Rain highlight colour is set separately.
